"For Aberdeen's Pat Connaughton, baseball to take back seat this week," ''The Baltimore Sun'', Tuesday, July 29, 2014.] born January 6, 1993) is an American professional [[basketball]] player for the [[Charlotte Hornets]] of the [[National Basketball Association]] (NBA), where he primarily plays as a [[shooting guard]]. He is also a former professional [[baseball]] player. Connaughton previously played for the [[Notre Dame Fighting Irish baseball]] and [[Notre Dame Fighting Irish men's basketball|men's basketball]] teams. He was selected by the [[Baltimore Orioles]] in the fourth round of the [[2014 MLB draft]]. The [[Brooklyn Nets]] selected him in the second round of the [[2015 NBA draft]] and traded him to the [[Portland Trail Blazers]]. In 2021, during his sixth season in the NBA, he won [[2021 NBA Finals|a championship]] with the [[Milwaukee Bucks]].{{Cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/stats/player/1626192/|title = Pat Connaughton| website=[[NBA.com]] }} ==High school career== Connaughton attended [[St. John's Preparatory School (Massachusetts)|St. John's Preparatory School]] in [[Danvers, Massachusetts]], where he starred in three sports, playing [[quarterback]] in [[American football|football]] and multiple positions in both baseball and basketball.{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/story/_/id/12133309/notre-dame-fighting-irish-senior-pat-connaughton-dual-sport-athlete-torn-basketball-baseball |title=Connaughton's dual-sport decision |first=Jeff |last=Goodman |work=[[ESPN.com]] |date=January 9, 2015 |access-date=January 9, 2015}} He received major interest in baseball from schools in the [[National Collegiate Athletic Association]] (NCAA) [[NCAA Division I|Division I]], with [[Boston College]] (BC), the [[University of Virginia]], and his original first choice, the [[University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill]], who all made him scholarship offers. Connaughton's sporting trajectory changed during the summer between his junior and senior years. At that time, he had only received a basketball offer from home-state [[Bentley University]], in NCAA's [[NCAA Division II|Division II]]. He suddenly emerged as a major basketball prospect after what ''[[ESPN.com]]'' writer Jeff Goodman called "one spectacular week" at the [[Amateur Athletic Union]] national tournament in [[Orlando, Florida]], including a game where he had 33 [[point (basketball)|points]] and 20 [[rebound (basketball)|rebounds]]. Connaughton himself would later say, "That week completely changed my entire life." He then began receiving multiple offers in basketball as well as baseball, with many schools willing to let him play both sports. He eventually chose the [[University of Notre Dame]] over [[Boston College|BC]], the [[University of Miami]], the [[University of California, Los Angeles]], and [[Vanderbilt University]]. In 2011, Connaughton's senior year, he was named the [[Gatorade Player of the Year awards|Gatorade Massachusetts Boys Basketball Player of the Year]].{{cite web|url=https://www.boston.com/yourtown/news/danvers/2011/03/pat_connaughton_is_the_gatorad.html|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150110044748/http://www.boston.com/yourtown/news/danvers/2011/03/pat_connaughton_is_the_gatorad.html|url-status=dead|archive-date=January 10, 2015|title=Pat Connaughton is the Gatorade Massachusetts Boys Basketball Player of the Year|first=Ayoub |last=Kourikchi|work=Boston Globe|date=March 18, 2011|access-date=June 13, 2014}} As a [[pitcher]] for the baseball team, he had an 11–2 [[win–loss record (pitching)|win–loss record]] with a 1.75 [[earned run average]] (ERA) and 160 [[strikeout]]s in 90 [[innings pitched]] as a senior. According to the baseball scouting site ''Perfect Game'', Connaughton was rated as the 33rd-best player in [[2011 Major League Baseball Draft|that year's]] [[Major League Baseball]] (MLB) [[Major League Baseball draft|draft]], but he fell to the 4th round, where he was selected by the [[San Diego Padres]], when he made it clear he planned to attend college. He followed through on his commitment to Notre Dame, choosing not to sign with the Padres. ==College career== At Notre Dame, Connaughton played for the [[Notre Dame Fighting Irish]] as a member of their [[college baseball]] and [[college basketball]] teams. In [[2011–12 Notre Dame Fighting Irish men's basketball team|his freshman year]] for the basketball team, Connaughton was one of three players to appear in all of Notre Dame's 34 games. He averaged 7.0 [[points per game]], 4.4 [[rebounds per game]], and 0.9 [[assists per game]] while playing 24.1 [[minutes per game]]. The Fighting Irish appeared in the [[2012 NCAA Men's Division I Basketball Tournament]], but lost to [[2011–12 Xavier Musketeers men's basketball team|Xavier University]] in the second round. Connaughton scored 10 points with two assists and two rebounds in 34 minutes of play during the loss. He agreed to terms with the Orioles, receiving a signing bonus of over $400,000, with the Orioles permitting Connaughton to play basketball for the Irish in his senior year.{{cite magazine|url=https://www.si.com/basketball/2014/06/09/pat-connaughton-baltimore-orioles-contract-notre-dame |title=Orioles to allow Pat Connaughton to play basketball for Notre Dame|via=[[Associated Press]]|magazine=[[Sports Illustrated]] |date=June 9, 2014 |access-date=June 13, 2014}}{{cite web|agency=Associated Press|url=http://www.indystar.com/story/sports/2014/06/09/notre-dames-pat-connaughton-will-play-two-sports/10260889/ |title=Notre Dame's Pat Connaughton will play two sports |work=[[Indianapolis Star]]|date=June 9, 2014 |access-date=June 13, 2014}} As a senior, Notre Dame's basketball team won its first [[Atlantic Coast Conference]] (ACC) championship. He took part in a 2015 tournament game against Kentucky for a [[NCAA Men's Division I Basketball Championship|Final Four]] berth, narrowly lost by his team after having sustained a lead until the six-second mark. Connaughton was determined to finish his degree at Notre Dame, and had a 3.0 [[Grading (education)|grade point average]] with the university's [[Mendoza College of Business]]. He ultimately graduated from Notre Dame in spring 2015. ==Professional baseball career== Connaughton made his [[professional baseball]] debut with the [[Aberdeen IronBirds]] of the [[Class A-Short Season|Low-A]] [[New York–Penn League]], in which he registered a {{convert|96|mph}} [[fastball]].{{cite web|url=http://www.southbendtribune.com/sports/professional/pro-baseball-connaughton-makes-professional-debut/article_05292dea-029a-11e4-9c8c-001a4bcf6878.html|title=Pro baseball: Connaughton makes professional debut|work=South Bend Tribune|access-date=January 11, 2015}} At the end of July 2014, he left the IronBirds to return to the Fighting Irish basketball team.{{cite web|url=https://www.baltimoresun.com/2014/07/29/for-aberdeens-pat-connaughton-baseball-to-take-back-seat-this-week/|title=For Aberdeen's Pat Connaughton, baseball to take backseat this week |work=[[The Baltimore Sun]]|first=Alejandro |last=Zuniga|date=July 29, 2014|access-date=January 11, 2015}} Even though the Orioles allowed him to pursue an NBA career, they never made any attempts to recoup the $428,000 [[signing bonus]]. As a result, the ballclub continued to control his contractual baseball rights through 2020, which could have been extended for six additional years if Baltimore placed him on its major league roster.[https://www.baltimoresun.com/2016/01/18/nbas-pat-connaughton-an-orioles-draft-pick-believes-he-will-eventually-return-to-baseball/ Encina, Eduardo A. "NBA's Pat Connaughton, an Orioles draft pick, believes he will eventually return to baseball," Monday, January, 18, 2016.] The Orioles did not add him to their major league roster in that span, meaning Connaughton would be free to sign with any team if he decided to return to baseball. ==Professional basketball career== ===Portland Trail Blazers (2015–2018)=== Connaughton was drafted with the 41st pick by the [[Brooklyn Nets]] in the [[2015 NBA draft]]. His draft rights, along with [[Mason Plumlee]], were then traded to the [[Portland Trail Blazers]] for [[Steve Blake]] and the draft rights to the 23rd pick in the draft, [[Rondae Hollis-Jefferson]].{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/blazers/trail-blazers-acquire-mason-plumlee-draft-rights-pat-connaughton-brooklyn|title=Trail Blazers Acquire Mason Plumlee, Draft Rights to Pat Connaughton from Brooklyn|work=NBA.com|publisher=Turner Sports Interactive, Inc.|date=June 25, 2015|access-date=June 25, 2015}} He signed a three-year deal with the Trail Blazers on July 9.{{cite web|title=Trail Blazers Sign Pat Connaughton|url=http://www.nba.com/blazers/trail-blazers-sign-pat-connaughton|work=NBA.com|date=July 8, 2015|access-date=July 13, 2015}} The first two years of the contract were guaranteed, with the stipulation that Connaughton would not be allowed to play professional baseball during that timespan.[https://www.nytimes.com/2016/03/07/sports/basketball/being-paid-to-play-basketballpat-connaughton-is-dreaming-of-diamonds.html?_r=0 Waldstein, David. "Being Paid to Play Basketball, Pat Connaughton Is Dreaming of Diamonds," ''The New York Times'', Monday, March 7, 2016.] He made his debut for the Trail Blazers on October 30, 2015, scoring five points in a loss to the [[Phoenix Suns]].{{cite web|title=Bledsoe, Knight lead Suns to 110–92 win over Portland|url=http://www.nba.com/games/20151030/PORPHX/gameinfo.html|work=NBA.com|date=October 30, 2015|access-date=October 30, 2015}} He appeared in 34 games for the Trail Blazers as a rookie.[http://www.oregonlive.com/blazers/index.ssf/2016/07/trail_blazers_pat_connaughton_wants_to_prove_he_is.html Trail Blazers' Pat Connaughton wants to prove he is more than just a great athlete] On April 13, 2017, in the Blazers' 2016–17 season finale, Connaughton scored a then career-high 19 points in a 103–100 loss to the [[New Orleans Pelicans]].{{cite 32.3 || .450 || .386 || .777 || 5.9 || 1.8 || .7 || .5 || 10.5 {{S-end}} ==Personal life== In Goodman's 2015 story on Connaughton and his decision between two sports, many key individuals in his life testified to his character. His father Len noted, "Patrick is of high moral character and wasn't going to lie to people. That eliminated a bunch of [MLB] teams from taking him at all." Notre Dame head basketball coach [[Mike Brey]] added, "In my 15 years here, no one has been more responsible than Pat Connaughton. He's an unbelievable ambassador for us and has shown tremendous loyalty." Family adviser Sam Samardzija, brother of former [[San Francisco Giants]] pitcher and former Notre Dame baseball and [[Notre Dame Fighting Irish football|football]] star [[Jeff Samardzija]], said about Connaughton, "He's not common—kind of like Jeff and [NFL quarterback] [[Russell Wilson]]. Not a lot of guys like him come around. He's just wired differently." Connaughton said he only allowed himself one luxury with his signing bonus, buying a new [[Jeep Wrangler]]. He told Goodman, "The signing bonus is a ton of money, especially for a 21-year-old. But I'm not going to live off that money. At some point, I'm going to live off a college degree." Connaughton is the president of a development firm.
